note: All three measured across three tiers; nine notebooks, five results CSVs.

note: M5/M6/M8, kappa in {1, 10, 1e2, 1e3, 1e4}; M6 stress-tested to 1e8.

note: M9, google/ddpm-cifar10-32 on a Kaggle T4.

item: Efficiency frontier in NFE, not wall-clock
note: Paper Table 7: runtime is linear in NFE and near-identical across solvers, so wall-clock carries no extra information.

item: Tier-1 kappa sweep at fixed d, not the deck's d = 2..100 sweep
note: The linear case decouples into d independent scalar ODEs -- dimension changes nothing. (Guide, Part 3, item 1.)

item: Tier 2 point/Gaussian mixture, not a Swiss roll
note: A continuous Swiss-roll density has no closed-form score; the deck claims one. M7 uses swiss_roll(n=8) as mixture *centers*, which does.

item: DOP853 reference at rtol 1e-13, not 1e-14
note: SciPy rejects rtol below ~2.2e-14. Convergence verified by recomputing at 1e-11 (agreement 6.9e-13, far below every measured error).

item: Authors' DPM-Solver code + analytic oracle, not a reimplementation
note: Tests the real published implementation with zero model error, and removes a week of work. Gate G1 pins the two together to 5.5e-16.

item: Tier-3 checkpoint google/ddpm-cifar10-32, targets paper Table 4
note: One-line download instead of fragile Drive links. The deck's 4.70 FID target is from a different (continuous VP-deep) checkpoint.

item: RK45 / adaptive solver
note: Step size is not a free variable for an adaptive method, so 'order vs h' and 'max stable h' are not defined on it. AB2 restores the deck's multistep row.

item: FID-5k vs NFE on Tier 3 (as an anchor to the paper, not the grading metric)
note: Cut at Gate G2, restored by M11 after the review: 5k samples at 10 and 20 NFE for six samplers plus a converged run; rankings compared with paper Table 6. The FID floor (notebook 11b) measures how much of the absolute value is sample size.

item: FID-50k as the primary Tier-3 metric
note: 50k x 35 configs is roughly ten GPU-hours the project did not have.

item: Arm B (the lambda-reparameterised ODE)
note: Separates DPM-Solver's two ideas: A vs B isolates the reparameterisation, B vs C isolates the exact linear treatment.

item: Gate G1 (DDIM == DPM-Solver-1 to machine precision)
note: Measured 5.5e-16 against a 1e-14 bar; catches broken lambda handling before anything downstream is built.

item: The crossover study (M8, M12.3)
note: Where order 3 overtakes order 1: at matched step size (M8) and at matched NFE (M12.3), the paper's own comparison. On the real checkpoint DPM-3 overtakes DPM-1 at ~14 NFE -- the unexplained Table-6 anomaly, reproduced and located.

item: Three-way Tier-3 error decomposition
note: Discretization / t_end truncation / network+precision floor, separated and measured (M9 section 7).

item: Sample-image grids (the paper's Figure 4, on our checkpoint)
note: M11: the project's first generated images. At 10 NFE DPM-2 produces sharp but different pictures -- why it loses on L2 and wins on FID.

item: Matched-protocol controls (M12.1)
note: Tiers 1-2 re-run under Tier 3's own settings: separates the NFE band's effect on measured order from the network's.

item: When DPM-Solver's split helps (M12.4)
note: A data-variance sweep: the exact linear treatment helps on concentrated data and hurts on spread-out data, where the t-form right-hand side cancels exactly.

item: FID floor at small sample counts (notebook 11b)
note: Real held-out CIFAR-10 images scored with M11's exact FID call at 1k-10k: the best FID any sampler could get at M11's sample size.
